name: Forehead Texture
mechanism:
This method analyzes forehead skin texture for deepfake detection:

1. **Forehead Region Extraction**: The forehead region is segmented per frame — bounded by hairline, eyebrows, and temples. This region is geometrically normalized to compensate for head tilt and provide consistent texture analysis across frames.

2. **Multi-Scale Texture Analysis**: Forehead texture is analyzed at multiple scales: macro (expression wrinkles, vein visibility), meso (pores, fine wrinkles), and micro (skin grain, peach fuzz). Natural foreheads exhibit characteristic texture at each scale. AI-generated foreheads often show texture quality that drops off at finer scales.

3. **Expression-Texture Correlation**: Forehead texture changes predictably with expressions — horizontal wrinkles appear with brow raising (frontalis contraction), vertical wrinkles with brow furrowing (corrugator contraction). The method verifies that texture changes correlate correctly with detected expressions. Deepfakes may show expression without corresponding wrinkle formation.

4. **Sweat/Sebum Indicator Analysis**: Real foreheads show subtle specular highlights from skin oils/perspiration, with characteristic spatial distribution. The method detects these physiological indicators — AI generators typically don't model skin surface moisture, producing either uniformly matte or uniformly shiny foreheads.

5. **Temporal Texture Stability**: Fine forehead texture (pore positions, stable wrinkles) should remain fixed across frames. The method tracks micro-texture consistency — frame-to-frame variations in pore patterns or shifting wrinkle positions indicate per-frame independent rendering by AI generators.
parameters:
Analysis type: pixel
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through forehead texture analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video

references.title: Rossler, A. et al. (2019). FaceForensics++: Learning to Detect Manipulated Facial Images. ICCV.
